road-bike.definition: A lightweight bicycle designed mainly for efficient riding on paved roads.
road-bike.exampleUsage: The road bike has narrow tires and drop handlebars.

mountain-bike.definition: A bicycle built with a reinforced frame and broad tires, first developed for travel across mountainous terrain.

bmx.definition: A BMX is a compact, sturdy bicycle first developed for bicycle motocross, with twenty-inch wheels suited to jumps and stunt riding.

cruiser.definition: A car in which policemen cruise the streets.

folding-bike.definition: A bicycle designed with hinges or joints so it can fold into a smaller size for storage or transport.
folding-bike.exampleUsage: The folding bike fits into a small storage area.

electric-bike.definition: A bicycle equipped with an electric motor that assists pedaling or propulsion under local rules.
electric-bike.exampleUsage: The electric bike uses a rechargeable battery.

kids-bike.definition: A bicycle sized and designed for children.
kids-bike.exampleUsage: The kids bike has a smaller frame.

cargo-bike.definition: A bicycle designed to carry larger loads, often using an extended frame, box, or cargo rack.
cargo-bike.exampleUsage: The cargo bike carried groceries in its front box.

wheel.definition: Game equipment consisting of a wheel with slots that is used for gambling.

chain.definition: A series of things depending on each other as if linked together.

pedal.definition: Of or relating to the feet.

handlebar.definition: The shaped bar used to steer a bicycle.

seat.definition: Any support where you can sit (especially the part of a chair or bench etc. on which you sit).

brake.definition: To stop travelling by applying a brake.

gear.definition: A toothed wheel that engages another toothed mechanism in order to change the speed or direction of transmitted motion.

spoke.definition: Support consisting of a radial member of a wheel joining the hub to the rim.

frame.definition: The supporting shape or structure of a building.

helmet.definition: A hard covering worn to protect the head.

light.definition: Not great in degree or quantity or number.

bell.definition: A device that makes a ringing sound.

basket.definition: The quantity contained in a basket.

rack.definition: A support for displaying or holding various articles.

water-bottle.definition: A container used for carrying drinking water.

phone-mount.definition: A holder that secures a phone to a bicycle or other surface so it can remain visible without being held.
phone-mount.exampleUsage: The phone mount was fixed securely to the handlebar before the ride.

jersey.definition: A breed of dairy cattle developed on the island of Jersey.

shorts.definition: Accidental contact between two points in an electric circuit that have a potential difference.

gloves.definition: The handwear used by fielders in playing baseball.

shoes.definition: A restraint provided when the brake linings are moved hydraulically against the brake drum to retard the wheel's rotation.

sunglasses.definition: (plural) spectacles that are darkened or polarized to protect the eyes from the glare of the sun.

rain-jacket.definition: A waterproof or water-resistant jacket designed to protect the wearer from rain.
rain-jacket.exampleUsage: The cyclist packed a rain jacket.

reflective-vest.definition: A high-visibility vest with reflective material that helps make the wearer easier to see.
reflective-vest.exampleUsage: The cyclist wore a reflective vest in low light.

arm-warmers.definition: Close-fitting fabric sleeves worn on the arms for extra warmth during cycling or other activities.
arm-warmers.exampleUsage: The rider added arm warmers on the cool morning.

leg-warmers.definition: Close-fitting fabric coverings worn on the legs for extra warmth.
leg-warmers.exampleUsage: The cyclist wore leg warmers in cold weather.

wrench.definition: A tool used for turning nuts, bolts, or pipes.

tire-lever.definition: A small bicycle tool used by trained or knowledgeable users to help remove a tire from a wheel rim.
tire-lever.exampleUsage: The repair kit included a tire lever.

patch-kit.definition: A small set of materials intended for repairing a punctured bicycle inner tube.
patch-kit.exampleUsage: The bicycle bag contained a patch kit.

multi-tool.definition: A compact tool that combines several bicycle-maintenance functions in one device.
multi-tool.exampleUsage: The cyclist carried a small multi-tool for routine maintenance.

chain-tool.definition: A specialized bicycle tool used to remove, install, or adjust chain pins or links.
chain-tool.exampleUsage: The mechanic kept a chain tool at the repair bench.

stand.definition: A stop made by a touring musical or theatrical group to give a performance.

spoke-wrench.definition: A small bicycle tool used to turn spoke nipples when adjusting wheel-spoke tension.
spoke-wrench.exampleUsage: The workshop has a spoke wrench for professional wheel service.

cable.definition: A conductor for transmitting electrical or optical signals or electric power.

brake-pad.definition: A replaceable pad presses against one side of a rotating brake disk, creating friction that slows the wheel.

bike-lane.definition: A lane for bicycles that uses curbs, posts, or similar barriers to keep riders apart from moving traffic.

trail.definition: A path through a natural area for walking.

hill.definition: An area of land that rises above the surrounding ground.

turn.definition: A circular segment of a curve.

signal.definition: An electrical or radio message that carries information.

park.definition: A gear position that acts as a parking brake.

lock-up.definition: Secure a place or object by fastening its lock.

flat-tire.definition: An air-filled tire that has lost enough pressure to become unusable.
